title: Policy-driven Terraform healer for VPC probe failures and safe upgrades
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: recurring VPC node probe regressions (probe timeouts, TTL/KV divergence, and intermittent kernel OOMs) cause degraded routing, throttled capacity, and manual operator toil. Goal: ship a policy-driven Terraform + orchestration-based remediation system ("Healer") that can safely repair common Private deployment healthcheck failures, gate automated repairs with preflight checks, and provide a deterministic rollback path for upgrades.
detection_signals: kv-cache-delta: node reports cache version mismatch compared to cohort leader (staled_kv_count > 10)
remediation_steps: Automated (first-tier): invoke healer-controller with safe policy: run preflight checks -> lock Terraform state -> create replacement node (create_before_destroy) with matching tags -> wait for probe success -> gracefully drain and decommission old node.
Circuit-breaker: do not execute if cluster-wide probe failures exceed 20% or active incidents > 1 (requires manual approval).
Manual remediation: run 'infra ops diagnostic <node-id>' to collect logs, KV cache snapshot, and kernel logs; escalate to on-call if root cause not surfaced within 20 minutes.
Rollback: if node replacement causes increased error rates, run terraform state rollback via stored snapshots and trigger canary rollback policy to previous image/build for up to 30 minutes.
Post-remediation: run KV cache reconciliation job and warm KV prefixes for tail-latency-sensitive models; mark run in audit log with operator and changelist.
Notifications: heal events produce structured alerts to PagerDuty + Slack channel #private-ops with remediation run id and relevant graphs.
Safe tainting: only taint nodes via automation; disallow manual 'terraform taint' unless acknowledged in ticketing system.
terraform_changes: Introduce module 'vpc_node_healer' with an optional lifecycle block using create_before_destroy to ensure replacement resources are created before old ones are destroyed.
Add taintable resource wrapper that records 'heal_reason' in Terraform state metadata to aid audits.
Add optional 'prevent_destroy' boolean toggles and a protected-tag pattern for customer-managed nodes to avoid accidental replacement.
Expose a 'preflight_script' hook for customers to provide custom readiness checks that run before node cutover.
Provide a lightweight plan-approve pipeline step that requires CI signature for production apply when auto-heal proposals modify more than N resources.
Add integration test harness for the module using localstack-like envs and a synthetic probe simulator.
upgrade_guards: Preflight matrix: terraform plan artifacts + golden probe-run verification on canary subset (5% of nodes) before global rollout.
Staged rollout: version pinning and exponential batch increases with health gates at 5m and 15m windows.
Fallback image pin: maintain last-known-good image tag for at least 48h after upgrade to enable quick revert.
Runtime feature flags: enable new healer behavior behind 'enable_vpc_healer' boolean to allow staged release per-customer.
Operator pause: automation will pause upgrades if KV cache divergence or TTL mismatches detected during rollout.
test_plan: Unit: terraform module unit tests validating lifecycle semantics and protect flags.
Integration: simulate probe timeouts in staging cluster and assert healer creates replacement node and passes probes within 10m.
Chaos: inject kernel oom and time-drift faults via fault-injector to validate heal/no-heal decision logic.
Performance: validate healer does not cause capacity drop > 5% during replacement under 95th percentile load.
Security: run plan-through-review to confirm no accidental exposure of customer KMS or private keys.
Runbook drill: on-call runbook drill (tabletop and live) with run id recording and postmortem.
monitoring_playbook: Alert runbook link: attach graph snapshots and healer run id to incident ticket automatically.
Cli snippets: 'infra healer status <run-id>' and 'infra healer abort <run-id>' documented for SREs.
Audit trail: store terraform plan/apply artifacts and healer logs in s3://redwood-infra-healer-logs/<run-id> for 90 days.
SLO considerations: label automated heals as 'zero-impact' only when replacement finishes within configured SLA window; otherwise increment incident counter.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy auto-heals could cascade and replace healthy nodes during cluster-wide flaps. Mitigation: global circuit-breaker and require cohort-local checks before replacement.
Risk: terraform state corruption on concurrent heals. Mitigation: strong state locks, per-cluster apply queues, and safe retries with exponential backoff.
Risk: customer dataplane disruption during PV attach/detach. Mitigation: create_before_destroy and attach-safety-wait hooks; require manual approval for nodes with non-ephemeral storage.
Risk: false positives from probe heuristics. Mitigation: improve signal fusion (heartbeat + kernel logs + kv-delta) and keep adjustable sensitivity per-customer.
acceptance_criteria: Automated heal runs in staging and fixes 90% of synthetic probe failures without manual intervention.
Healer logs include full terraform plan/artifact and a stable run id; artifacts retained for 90 days.
No increase in operational incidents attributed to healer in first 30 days post-release (measured weekly).
Upgrade guard prevents global rollout when KV divergence > threshold and requires manual override recorded in ticketing.
